summary: Unusual session activity after employee reported suspicious phishing email (triage & containment)
description: Issue reported by employee via #security-helpdesk: received a targeted phishing email, clicked a link, then observed an unexpected active session for their account from a foreign IP. This ticket documents triage steps, containment actions, and next steps for forensic analysis.
impact: Potential credential exposure for one SSO-enabled account. No confirmed lateral movement; some API keys associated with the user were briefly active before being revoked. A subset of internal console sessions were observed originating from a foreign IP (unknown device).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Employee received email with subject 'Invoice overdue - Redwood billing' containing shortened link. 2) Employee clicked link and was presented with a fake SSO prompt that resembled our Okta page. 3) Employee reported to #security-helpdesk at 2026-03-10T09:18:00Z. 4) Security observed a new session from IP 185.66.124.241 at 2026-03-10T09:22:10Z for the same user.
logs:
auth.log lines of interest (redacted):
- 2026-03-10T09:22:10Z AUTH SUCCESS user=j.smith ip=185.66.124.241 ua='Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)' session_id=abc123
- 2026-03-10T09:23:03Z SSO TOKEN ISSUE user=j.smith client_id=redwood-console token_id=tok-45f
- 2026-03-10T09:24:12Z API KEY USE key=redact-*** resource=api.v1.generate model=gpt-redwood-light
SIEM event id: SEV-7621. Packet capture reference: pcap-20260310-09-22 (stored in secure evidence bucket).

investigation_notes:
Preliminary findings: the phishing email used a legitimate-looking domain (redwood-billing[.]info) with a redirect through bit.ly. The SSO prompt was a credential-capture page that POSTed to a third-party domain. The session IP (185.66.124.241) geolocated to Eastern Europe and matches a set of previous malicious indicators (threat intel tag: THRT-2026-03-EU1).
No new service principals were created. The user did not approve any OAuth grants. API key usage observed came from the legitimate CLI token; timestamps show a brief window (09:24-09:27) before revocation. We found one suspicious header: X-Forwarded-For: 10.200.45.67 (internal range) which likely indicates proxy manipulation; need infra to confirm NAT logs.
Hypothesis: credentials were phished and used immediately from a foreign IP; attacker attempted to leverage active CLI token for quick API calls. No evidence of code exfiltration or model weights access.
mitigation_actions:
- Immediate actions (2026-03-10): forced password reset for j.smith, revoked all active sessions, rotated affected API tokens, disabled legacy CLI tokens, blocked IP 185.66.124.241 at WAF and infra ACLs, created SIEM watchrule for THRT-2026-03-EU1.
- Communication: notified user, sent company-wide advisory (no compromise detected beyond single account), posted summary to #security-ops and #incidents.
- Evidence preservation: captured session logs, exported relevant pcap, saved mailbox headers and the phishing message to secure bucket.
- Longer-term: SSO provider support ticket opened to review token issuance logs and phishing-resistant MFA options (push-based or hardware for admin tier).
resolution: Containment achieved: compromised account credentials invalidated, suspicious tokens rotated, and attacking IPs blocked. Forensics in progress (disk and memory imaging for the affected host). Postmortem scheduled; action items include improving phishing-resistant MFA rollout and updating the security awareness training to include this phishing template. Ticket remains In Progress until forensic report and postmortem are complete.
